long_biography.plain_text:
Michael Hill spent more than two decades in his uncle's Whangārei jewellery business, moving from watchmaking to sales and store management. After his newly built home burned down in 1977, he tried to buy the family shop. His uncle refused, so Hill and his wife, Christine, opened their own jewellery store in 1979.

The business distinguished itself through inviting layouts, focused product ranges and memorable advertising, then expanded across New Zealand, Australia and Canada. Hill later handed the chairmanship to his daughter Emma while remaining connected to the company. His abandoned ambition to become a concert violinist resurfaced in philanthropy: he later founded an international competition for emerging violinists. He was knighted for services to business and the arts.
